children: shares slipped about 2% in Friday morning trading despite the company outlining plans for electric air taxi networks across Austin, DallasFort Worth and Houston.

The proposed routes would connect major airports with commercial centers and popular destinations across the Texas Triangle, a region home to more than 20 million people. Archer sees the networks as a potential alternative to road travel in an area facing growing traffic congestion.

The company estimates its all-electric Midnight aircraft could reduce journeys that take 60 to 90 minutes by car to flights lasting just 10 to 20 minutes. The proposed service aims to make regional transportation faster while linking key business and travel destinations.

In DallasFort Worth, the network would connect six airports with business locations, including Frisco Station. Houston routes would link three airports with a downtown hotel helipad and Galveston. In Austin, planned connections include two airports and the Circuit of The Americas racing venue.

Chief Executive Adam Goldstein said the proposed networks are designed to improve connections between major destinations and reduce time spent in traffic. The company did not provide a launch timeline in the supplied information.

title: Archer Aviation Stock Falls Despite Major Texas Air Taxi Expansion Plans
